note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them”. In all of our affliction, through all of our slavery, the Lord saw all of it.

In all our affliction he was afflicted. So when he comes back, he is going to feel all of that pain and all of that suffering they did to the children of Israel, and he is going to wreak havoc on these nations.

“the angel of his presence saved them”. Salvation is not for the oppressors. Salvation is for those who have been afflicted. The man that ruled over another did it to his own hurt, because the one he afflicted is the one the Lord saves.

precepts.point: Israel shall be named priests of the Lord, receive double for its shame, and its seed shall be known among the Gentiles.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Isaiah 61 proclaims “the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God.” There is a particular day in a particular year when God will come to deliver his people. Isaiah 63 shows that day: “Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength?” This is Christ, the Son of God, and his garment is glorious, not a sheet or a robe.

“Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat?” Isaiah is asking Christ, Why are you red? It looks like you were stomping grapes. “I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me.” Christ trod down the nations and killed them alone. He did not need the help of the twelve tribes of Israel; he did it himself.

“for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments.” The wine represents their blood.

“For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.” We are the redeemed. The year of my redeemed is the acceptable year of the Lord in Isaiah 61, our jubilee, and it comes with the day of vengeance on the nations.

note.label: Mistakes We Make in This Truth

precepts.text: Doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Israel acknowledge us not: thou, O Lord, art our father, our redeemer; thy name is from everlasting. Reconciled. Reconciled who? To what? Married people get reconciled. They were together under a covenant. Something happened. They broke apart. And then, in order to bring the marriage back together, they must reconcile. That is what that means. The nation of Israel was once together under God. Something happened. Then Christ brought them back together.
precepts.point: So reconcile means to restore friendly relations. I have a question. When was God ever on friendly terms with the other nations?

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
“Doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Israel acknowledge us not: thou, O Lord, art our father, our redeemer; thy name is from everlasting.” The Lord is Israel’s father and Israel’s redeemer, from everlasting.

Reconciled: reconciled who, to what? Married people get reconciled. They were together under a covenant, something happened and they broke apart, and in order to bring the marriage back together they must reconcile. That is what the word means.

The nation of Israel was once together under God, as the children of their father. Something happened: sin and the split of the kingdoms. Then Christ brought them back together. That is why Ephesians says he might “reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross”: both kingdoms brought back to the Father who was always theirs.

precepts.text: We are thine: thou never barest rule over them; they were not called by thy name. We are thine. Thou never barest rule over them. God never bore rule over the other nations. So how can you reconcile to a God that never owned you, that never knew you, that never had you?
precepts.point: So reconcile means to restore friendly relations. I have a question. When was God ever on friendly terms with the other nations?

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
“We are thine: thou never barest rule over them; they were not called by thy name.” Israel says to the Lord, we are yours. And of the other nations: the Lord never bore rule over them, and they were not called by His name.

So how can anyone be reconciled to a God that never owned them, never knew them, and never had them? To reconcile is to restore friendly relations that were there before. Israel was the Lord’s, called by His name, and fell away; the other nations never were His.

That is why the reconciling of Ephesians 2:16, “that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross,” belongs to Israel. The both are the two houses of Israel, the ones called by His name, brought back to the God who bore rule over them.

precepts.text: He that cometh from Bozrah with dyed garments has trodden the winepress alone; the garments washed in the blood of grapes look ahead to that day.
precepts.point: His eyes shall be red with wine: Christ drank wine, so much that men called him a winebibber, but he was never drunken.

note.label: Genesis 49: What Shall Befall the Twelve Tribes in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength? I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save.” Then: “Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat? I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me: for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment.”

That is where “he washed his garments in wine, and his clothes in the blood of grapes” runs ahead to: Christ returning from Bozrah with dyed garments, treading the winepress, to destroy Israel’s enemies. The blood of grapes on Judah’s clothes is the blood of the enemy sprinkled upon Christ’s garments in that day.

precepts.text: The great goodness toward the house of Israel; but they rebelled, and he was turned to be their enemy.
precepts.point: The letters of Paul were written to Israelites living in those lands and called by their names, Romans and Corinthians, the same way we are called American or Jamaican today; written today they would be the letter to the Jamaicans or the letter to the Puerto Ricans.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
Isaiah remembers “the great goodness toward the house of Israel, which he hath bestowed on them according to his mercies, and according to the multitude of his lovingkindnesses. For he said, Surely they are my people, children that will not lie: so he was their Saviour. In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bare them, and carried them all the days of old.”

“But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them.” Israel became the enemy of the Most High by sin. There are two kinds of enemies: the nations that are the natural enemies of the Most High, and Israel, who rebelled and vexed His holy spirit, and He was turned to be their enemy. That is why Israel needed a trespass offering and an atonement.

precepts.text: He that cometh from Edom with dyed garments from Bozrah treads the winepress in his fury, for the day of vengeance is in his heart and the year of his redeemed is come.
precepts.point: Out of Jacob shall come he that shall have dominion: that is the one who cometh from Edom with dyed garments from Bozrah, glorious in his apparel, traveling in the greatness of his strength, which is the whole host of heaven, thousands upon thousands of angels. The day of vengeance is in his heart, for though Israel serves out her punishment in captivity, Esau went overboard and kept laying on punishment when our iniquity had an end.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“Out of Jacob shall come he that shall have dominion, and shall destroy him that remaineth of the city.” That is the one who cometh from Edom. “Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength? I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save.” The greatness of his strength is the whole host of heaven, thousands upon thousands of angels.

“Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat? I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me: for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment.”

“For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.” The day of vengeance is in his heart, for though Israel serves out her punishment in captivity, Esau went overboard and kept laying on punishment when our iniquity had an end. He that has dominion out of Jacob destroys him that remaineth, and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau.

precepts.text: The people of thy holiness have possessed it but a little while; our adversaries have trodden down thy sanctuary.
precepts.point: Isaiah sums up Deuteronomy 28:1-14: we possessed it but a little while. Israel had the blessings to a point when they went into the land, but only about eighty years at the full level, under David and Solomon. How Solomon abounded in gold, ships, and plenty of food you can read in 1 Kings.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 28:1-14 is the blessings: the enemies that rise up against thee shall “flee before thee seven ways”; the blessing is commanded “in thy storehouses, and in all that thou settest thine hand unto”; the Most High establishes thee an holy people unto himself; all people of the earth see “that thou art called by the name of the Lord” and are afraid of thee; thou shalt lend unto many nations and not borrow; thou shalt be “the head, and not the tail”, above only and not beneath. All of it hangs on one condition: “if that thou hearken unto the commandments of the Lord thy God”, and turn not aside after other gods.

Isaiah sums up what became of it: “The people of thy holiness have possessed it but a little while: our adversaries have trodden down thy sanctuary.” Israel had the blessings to a point when they went into the land, but only about eighty years at the full level, under David and Solomon. How Solomon abounded in gold, ships and plenty of food you can read in 1 Kings. Then it was gone, and the adversaries trod down the sanctuary. We possessed it but a little while.

precepts.text: He was Israel's Savior and carried them all the days of old, but they rebelled and vexed his holy Spirit, therefore he was turned to be their enemy.
precepts.point: How did we repay all that kindness? But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them. The Most High had no choice but to turn against us, because we repaid him with rebellion.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“Do ye thus requite the Lord, O foolish people and unwise?” This is how you repay the magnificent Lord that delivered you, that destroyed whole nations just so you could inherit their land? “is not he thy father that hath bought thee? hath he not made thee, and established thee?” Isaiah recounts what there was to repay: “I will mention the lovingkindnesses of the Lord, and the praises of the Lord, according to all that the Lord hath bestowed on us, and the great goodness toward the house of Israel”.

“For he said, Surely they are my people, children that will not lie: so he was their Saviour. In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bare them, and carried them all the days of old.” Whenever he saw us going through atrocities he suffered with us. In his love and in his pity he redeemed us, and carried us all the days of old.

How did we repay all that kindness? “But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them.” The Most High had no choice but to turn against us, because we requited him with rebellion. That is the foolish people and unwise of the song.

precepts.text: The one who cometh from Edom with dyed garments, treading the winepress alone in the day of vengeance, is the same picture the song is singing of.
precepts.point: The Lord marching out of the field of Edom, the earth trembling, the heavens dropping, and the mountains melting from before the Lord God of Israel is future prophecy; this has not happened yet.

note.label: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People

precepts.why:
“Lord, when thou wentest out of Seir, when thou marchedst out of the field of Edom, the earth trembled, and the heavens dropped, the clouds also dropped water. The mountains melted from before the Lord.” This is future prophecy; this has not happened yet.

Isaiah sings of the same picture: “Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength?” The answer: “I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save.”

His garments are red because “I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me: for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment.” And the time is fixed: “For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.”

The one who marches out of the field of Edom in the song of Deborah is the one who comes from Edom with dyed garments, treading the winepress alone in the day of vengeance. The earth trembling and the mountains melting before the Lord God of Israel is that day.

precepts.text: He is Father and Redeemer to Israel; other nations were never called by His name.
precepts.point: The Most High controls the rain, the insects, and the pestilence. The people called by His name are Israel, the same people read through these chapters, and healing follows their humbling and turning, not a general love for all nations.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 7: Fire From Heaven and the Terms of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Israel acknowledge us not: thou, O Lord, art our father, our redeemer.” The Most High is Father and Redeemer to Israel, “the tribes of thine inheritance.”

Then the line that settles who “my people, which are called by my name” are: “We are thine: thou never barest rule over them; they were not called by thy name.” Other nations were never called by his name.

So the promise of 2 Chronicles 7:14 belongs to Israel, the same people read through these chapters. The Most High controls the rain, the locust and the pestilence, and the healing of the land follows Israel’s humbling, praying, seeking his face and turning from their wicked ways. It is not a general love for all nations.

precepts.text: In all their affliction He was afflicted and carried them, but they rebelled and vexed His holy Spirit, so He turned to be their enemy.
precepts.point: Even when He pitied us and provided everything, bearing us on His wings, we rebelled and vexed His Holy Spirit, so He turned to be our enemy.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
“God shall hear, and afflict them, even he that abideth of old. Selah. Because they have no changes, therefore they fear not God.” There was no change in us, no repentance. Isaiah tells how it went: “In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bare them, and carried them all the days of old.” He pitied us and provided everything, bearing us on his wings.

“But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them.” Even with all of that, we rebelled and vexed his Holy Spirit, so he turned to be our enemy. That is why he afflicts: because they have no changes.

precepts.text: He comes from Edom with dyed garments, having trodden the winepress alone, treading them in His anger so their blood is sprinkled on His raiment, for the day of vengeance is in His heart.
precepts.point: The Most High is going to lay His vengeance upon Edom by the hand of His people Israel, His battle axe, and there will be so much death that everyone has to pitch in and bury them for seven months. That is a beautiful thing.

note.label: Psalm 58: The Righteous Shall Rejoice When He Seeth the Vengeance

precepts.why:
“The righteous shall rejoice when he seeth the vengeance: he shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked.” Isaiah sees who comes from that vengeance: “Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength? I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save.” He comes from Edom with dyed garments.

“Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat? I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me: for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment.” He treads Edom in his anger so their blood is sprinkled on his raiment. “For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.” That is the vengeance the righteous rejoice to see, and the blood of the wicked they wash their feet in.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
The precept about his garment being dipped in blood: it said he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood, and Isaiah said the same thing. “Who is this that cometh from Edom”, put the map with Edom up, “this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength? I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save.”

“Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel”: why you got all that blood on your clothes? “And thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat?”

“I have trodden the winepress alone”: you know when you tread in the winepress you’re stomping grapes. Christ said, I did all the killing of people by myself. “And of the people there was none with me”: I didn’t need none of you people, none of you Israelites, to help me at all.

“For I will tread them in” my anger, “and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments”: y’all see that? So when Christ comes he’s doing a whole lot of what, brothers? Killing. “And I will stain all my raiment.” Then back to Revelation 19:13: “And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.”

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

precepts.why:
Somebody says God don’t respect nobody, God is no respecter of persons. Read it: “And God looked upon the children of Israel, and God had respect unto them.” God had respect unto them, and God has respect unto us. He looked at what he made and said, that looks good right there, I respect that.

When the Bible says no respect of persons, it means that among us, brothers, rank don’t matter. If one is a king and the other an hourly worker at a job, the Lord will judge the king for his evil the same way he will judge the worker. Anybody can get it: King David got it, King Saul got it, King Solomon got it; all the forefathers that were great men still got some judgment at one point in their life. So there is no respect of persons with God, but as far as the children of Israel are concerned, God had respect unto them. That is the God who in all their affliction was afflicted.

note.label: SABBATH MORNING CLASS: Apollos Creed

precepts.why:
“Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength? I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save. Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat?” Remember how we make wine: you step on the grapes, and all of the juices fly up on you.

“I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me”: I went in there and did that work all by myself, nobody was with me. “For I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury”: who’s being trampled? Edom. “And their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments”.

That’s the vesture dipped in blood. Go back to Revelation 19:13: “And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.” Now we know who the Word is: Christ. That’s how you’re going to be able to break this stuff down. Y’all sit around playing Assassin’s Creed; this is Apollos Creed.

note.label: BLACK ALLIANCE WITH A SHADOW GOVERNMENT

precepts.why:
Who will lead God into Edom? “Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah?” Bozrah is the capital of Edom. “I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save”: that is Christ.

“Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat?” Isaiah asks why there is red all over his clothes, as if he had been stomping grapes. “I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me”: I don’t need the Israelites to help me. “For I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment.” He will tread Edom in his anger.

So the Son of God knows exactly who he is coming back to fight. Edom is not done away with.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

precepts.why: “Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah?” “Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel”: why does it look like grape juice is all on your clothes, Lord? “I have trodden the winepress alone”: the winepress is the Earth. “And of the people there was none with me”: of the Israelites there was none to help; God didn’t need your help. “For I will tread them in mine anger”: verse one tells you who; Edom is America, Edom is the EU, France, Germany. “And their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments”: the wine Isaiah thought it was is blood. “For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 19 Supper, War & Marriage

That’s the day we’re looking for: let every wicked thing be put to death. If you ain’t trying to roll with this, I’d rather see you dead than see you trespass these commandments. “And the year of my redeemed is come.” Bishop: that was good.

note.label: Gods Memorial: The Smoke of Her Torment

precepts.why:
I could go to the New Testament and show you all that too, because we got some Christians lurking. When I said Christ is going to kill the Europeans you all are thinking, this dude is racist and hateful; read Revelation 19.

“And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.” This man’s garment is gonna be dipped in blood, and his name is called the Word of God, so we know this is talking about Christ. “And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses”: that’s all angels, “clothed in fine linen, white and clean.”

“And out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations”: Christ is going to destroy the nations, nations like Greece, Turkey, Germany, Russia, Great Britain, Portugal. He ain’t coming to give the nations hugs and kisses. “And he shall rule them with a rod of iron: and he treadeth the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of Almighty God.” This is the same thing we read in Isaiah 63: for those of you all saying that’s the Old Testament, it’s revealing the same thing in the New Testament. “And he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.”

“Come and gather yourselves together unto the supper of the great God”. What kind of supper is this? This isn’t like the Last Supper that Christ had with the apostles. This is a different supper: all nations is invited, and guess what, they are the food. God is going to call a great supper for the fowls of the heaven. “That ye may eat the flesh of kings”: that king in Saudi Arabia, the new king in Britain, Prince Charles, all of these kings and rulers. “And the flesh of captains”: the captains are the armies; “and the flesh of mighty men”: all the mighty soldiers; “and the flesh of horses, and of them that sit on them, and the flesh of all men, both free and bond, both small and great.” Everybody getting killed when Christ return.

“And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse, and against his army.” The beast is that fourth beast, the Caucasian race, Europe. They’re gonna make war with Christ. Europe is not going to embrace Christ when he return; they’re gonna make war with him.

“And the beast was taken”: the white man will be destroyed; that beast is the seven heads and ten horns. “And with him the false prophet”: the false prophet is Christianity, “that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast”. Those of you all that believe Jesus is white, or it doesn’t matter what color Jesus is, Jesus love all the children, those of you that think like that have been deceived, and you’re gonna be destroyed along with the so-called white man. Some of you online can’t stand what I’m saying, even though we’re reading it.

“And them that worshipped his image”: that white image right there is the image of the beast. The image of the beast is another Jesus, the one written about in Matthew 24, ‘many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ’. That’s the white man setting himself up as Christ: that fourth beast speaking great words against the most High by setting himself up as Christ.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 14 Part 2

precepts.why:
Isaiah says the same thing about the grapes being crushed and smashed and reaped. “Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel”: when the Bible says Christ had on a white garment, it was glorious, not a sheet, not a toga; the most decked-out garment you can imagine.

“Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat?” Like in Italy, where they go into the winepress and smash the grapes with their feet and the juice splashes everywhere: Isaiah is asking Christ in his vision why he looks like he just came out of crushing grapes.

“I have trodden the winepress alone”: I have killed the nations alone. “And of the people there was none with me”: no Israelites helping him. “For I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment. For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.”

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

precepts.why:
“Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah?” From Bozrah, not too far from the Mount of Olives. “This that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength? I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save. Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel”: why are your garments covered in red? “And thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat?”

“I have trodden the winepress alone”: I’m going to do it alone; I don’t need help. “And of the people there was none with me: for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment. For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come”: the year of our redemption.

points: We are thine: thou never barest rule over them; they were not called by thy name. You see that: the nations were never called by God's name. The name he gave us is Israel. God's name is on us.

note.label: Mistakes We Make in This Truth

points: The beginning of Isaiah 63 is straight vengeance: Isaiah saw Christ coming with a vengeance, destroying our enemies. Then the chapter takes a turn: “I will mention the lovingkindnesses of the Lord, and the praises of the Lord, according to all that the Lord hath bestowed on us, and the great goodness toward the house of Israel.” Great goodness toward who? The house of Israel. That goodness the Lord has extended, and is going to continue to extend, to the house of Israel. Don’t let anybody fool you. He bestowed it “according to his mercies, and according to the multitude of his lovingkindnesses.”

A sister on Clubhouse asked what the point of this life is: you’re just going to die, people are going to do you wrong. But where do you go when you die? We think when death comes it’s over. No, that’s just the beginning. If you die before Christ returns and you are not keeping his commandments, you are literally just waiting to be judged. But if you die in Christ keeping the commandments, you are going to be in paradise, and when his kingdom comes you are going to sit on the throne with him. Whoever asks what the point of this life is doesn’t understand their purpose, and doesn’t understand that there is a judgment after you die. That is what we have to make clear to our people, and what we are supposed to be living by.

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

points: “For he said, Surely they are my people”: what’s that word? Surely. So why are we walking around with our head hanging down? Why do we let people at our job make us feel insignificant? Why you let that no good negro tell you you ain’t no good? Some of you kids go to school and they mock you: keep your head high and carry yourself with grace. Brothers, we are the kings of this earth, and it’s time for us to understand that our sisters are the princesses of this earth. We should not be living like the world; we are better than that.

“Children that will not lie: so he was their Saviour.” He is going to save the nation of Israel; that’s a promise. Look how much we have been through as a nation and are still going through. The Bishops travel all over the world. Some of y’all never been to a third world country, and it’s real bad. You complain about the air condition; they have never felt an air condition. In the islands, like Grenada, they have single units in individual rooms; you better open a window or a door and get some breeze up in here. What we take for granted, our people in those countries have never experienced, but the Lord still says “Surely they are my people.”

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

points: “In all their affliction he was afflicted”: the Lord sees what they are doing to you, and it does piss him off. Everything we have gone through, the Lord himself was afflicted by it. Some people say God ain’t doing nothing, he don’t feel no type of way. A woman called God narcissistic: why does he think we should serve him? Maybe because your brain works and the blood is flowing through your veins right now. Your heart ain’t stopped; you have no disease that keeps you from walking or moving like some people out here; you can see and talk, and your body works like it’s supposed to. You have the power to get up and look at your children, the power even to have children. That is the reason you should be serving God. God ain’t narcissistic; he wants you to give him the respect he has given you. The Lord respected us enough to create us the greatest nation on earth.

“And the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bare them, and carried them all the days of old.” The Lord went and got our people out of Egypt. Egypt was the greatest nation on earth at that time, with the greatest military, all the wealth and all the wisdom, and the Lord destroyed that nation little by little, and for his final finale killed all their firstborn sons and let his children come out. At the very beginning of Exodus they were trying to kill our sons; then they took the brick and mortar from us and made us go out and get the straw, get the materials ourselves, and still meet the quota. Imagine your job sending you up on a roof to put up shingles with no shingles and no drill, and still wanting that roof up by sundown. That’s what they did to us. But by the end of us being in Egypt we came out of that thing shining. The Lord said give them all your gold, and we went in loin cloths getting our backs whipped and walked out of that thing bling blinging. That’s what your God does for you, and he ain’t forgot about us. He is going to do it again.

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

points: “Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah?” He is coming from the Caucasian race, from Edom. “Travelling in the greatness of his strength”: with all the armies of heaven. “I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save.”

note.label: The Evolution Of Revolutionaries

points: “Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat?” His garments look like someone who was stamping grapes. As Malcolm X said, there is no peaceful revolution. They will shed our blood, and our King will return and shed theirs.

note.label: The Evolution Of Revolutionaries

points: “I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me”: he destroys the nations by himself. “For I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury”: Europe, America and all the nations, because he is angry for what they have done. “And their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment.”

No turning the other cheek: Christ is coming for vengeance. We are not praying for their healing; we pray for Christ to return and stamp them like grapes. The Bible is a violent book. Some will call that hateful, but this is a nationalist and a revolutionist who loves his people. Stop always trying to save the heathen; get yourself together, stop the adultery, lying and stealing, and come back to the God of Israel.

note.label: The Evolution Of Revolutionaries

points: “For the day of vengeance is in mine heart”: vengeance belongs to the Lord, and the day of vengeance is in Christ’s hand. “And the year of my redeemed is come”: the year he redeems us from the lands where we were made slaves.

note.label: The Evolution Of Revolutionaries

points: “And I will tread down the people in mine anger”: the Europeans, the Arabs, the nations. “And I will bring down their strength to the earth”: their armies will be destroyed.

note.label: The Evolution Of Revolutionaries

points: “The great goodness toward the house of Israel, which he hath bestowed on them according to his mercies”. “For he said, Surely they are my people, children that will not lie: so he was their Saviour.” His people are Israel. Christ is our Saviour; he will save us and tread the nations. He is the biggest revolutionary.

He died a revolutionary death: they hanged our King on a tree, lynched him the way our forefathers died in slavery, and cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree. He died a black death, and that tells you our King is a black man.

note.label: The Evolution Of Revolutionaries

points: “In all their affliction he was afflicted”: everything the white man did and said to us, Christ felt, because we are one with our King and he dwells in us. That is why he is angry. “And the angel of his presence saved them”: that is Michael. “In his love and in his pity he redeemed them”.
Now the King has returned, and he is about to destroy all the nations. So do not be ashamed to be a revolutionary, and do not be afraid to be a nationalist.

note.label: The Evolution Of Revolutionaries

points: This is Christ coming to visit Edom. “Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah?” Bozrah is one of the capitals of Edom. “This that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength?” The greatness of his strength is all the angels with him. “I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save.”

note.label: Gods Memorial: The Smoke of Her Torment

points: “Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat?” This is Isaiah saying, why is your garment so dipped in blood?

note.label: Gods Memorial: The Smoke of Her Torment

points: “I have trodden the winepress alone”: who is the I here? The Lord Christ. Christ is going to go to Europe and he’s going to destroy; he’s gonna tread the winepress over there. Who is this coming from Bozrah? That’s where he’s coming from: he’s coming from all Europe. Christ is going to go over there and do a lot of killing.

“And of the people there was none with me”: Christ is going to say, listen, I don’t want none of you all to come with me, I gotta do this on my own; I don’t think you’re gonna be able to stand what I’m about to do.

“For I will tread them in mine anger”: the them here is the Europeans, Europe. “And trample them in my fury”. Why is Christ angry? Why is he so furious? Because of what they did to the children of Israel, his people, and what they are going to do to us in the near future. It could be five years from now, 10 years, 15 years, might be 20, but it’s not too far from now. When you watch the prophecy, we see Israel waking up, so we know what time we are in. The only thing we’re waiting on right now is for us to learn these laws and build ourselves up.

“And their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments”: Christ said, listen, the blood is gonna be sprinkled on my garment. I’m going to Europe and I’m going to be doing a lot of killing; that’s where all this blood on my garment come from, me killing Europeans. Isaiah said, why is your garment so dipped in blood? And Christ said, listen, I went over there and I had to do some killing, and I did it alone. Christ will become a mass murderer on this earth: he’s going to destroy all the armies, and then he’s going to go over into Europe and kill millions and millions of people. “And I will stain all my raiment.”

note.label: Gods Memorial: The Smoke of Her Torment

points: “For the day of vengeance is in mine heart”. Y’all better understand what Bible you are reading. Don’t be in la la land saying, oh, that’s the Old Testament.
